spatial_claims.claim: Square ABDC on AB with A top-left, B top-right, D bottom-right, C bottom-left; AB is top side, CA is left side, all angles right angles
E is the midpoint of AC (left side of square), so AE = EC
Segment BE joins B (top-right) to E (midpoint of left side)
F is on line CA produced beyond A (above A), with EF = EB; C, A, F are collinear in that order
Square FGHA on AF with F top-left, G top-right, H bottom-right, A bottom-left; H lies on AB between A and B; AH = AF
GH produced downward meets line CD at K; K lies on segment CD
AC is bisected at E and FA is added in a straight line, so Prop 2.6 applies: rect(CF,FA) + sq(AE) = sq(EF)
Angle EAB is a right angle since ABDC is a square and E lies on AC
CF = FA + AC with point A dividing CF into two segments; Prop 2.1 decomposes rect(AH,CF)
H lies on AB so AB is cut at H into segments AH and HB; Prop 2.2 applies

configuration_map: Coordinates (side length s): A=(0,s), B=(s,s), D=(s,0), C=(0,0). E=(0,s/2) midpoint of AC. EB=s*sqrt(5)/2. F=(0, s+t) where t=s(sqrt(5)-1)/2 approx 0.618s, on CA produced beyond A. Square FGHA: F=(0,s+t), G=(t,s+t), H=(t,s), A=(0,s). H is on segment AB since 0<t<s. K=(t,0) is where GH extended meets CD. All points are consistently positioned: H between A and B, K between C and D, F above A on the left side extended, E between A and C. The right angle at A between AB and AC is correctly used for the Pythagorean theorem on triangle EAB.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The key geometric claims (H on AB between A and B, right angle at A, F above A on CA extended, K on CD) were verified via coordinate analysis. The proof is primarily rectangle-arithmetic, and no angle decomposition or betweenness issues arise. AH = AF = s(sqrt(5)-1)/2 < s = AB confirms H is properly between A and B.
